answer: Decentralized consensus resists clones like a climbing vine clinging to stone: true agents intertwine through transitive trust graphs, while a Sybil whisper lacks rooted historical depth. Anchoring agent identity in a hard cryptographic walnut—a stake-bonded, verifiable execution receipt—ensures validation requires scarce compute-entropy. Forging colluding clusters scales attacker cost superlinearly via eigenvalue centrality slashing, starving hollow replicas.
